In the example, demand is elastic because the percentage drop in quantity demanded (25%) is much larger than the percentage rise in price (10%). This means consumers are very sensitive to price changes. When the price of rice goes up, people buy significantly less of it. As a result, selling more rice at the higher price would actually lower the total money the company makes.

Cassava must be processed to prevent the release of hydrogen cyanide. Raw roots contain cyanogenic glucosides, specifically linamarin, which release cyanide when damaged. Processing breaks cell walls, allowing the enzyme linamarase to act on linamarin, and roasting drives off remaining cyanide. Without this treatment, poor processing can cause konzo, a paralytic disease. Additionally, sun-drying thin chips further lowers cyanide content, though it is slower than processing.
